key_insight: Without an input promise, approximate quantum circuit membership is PP-hard across multiple target sets and distance metrics, implying PP-hardness of related circuit optimization tasks.
engineering_relevance: The results establish worst-case complexity barriers to minimizing total, non-Clifford, or superposition gate count and depth on hardware supporting Clifford+T.
method: Analyze promise-free membership near identity, Clifford-only sets, and generalized permutation sets.
Establish PP-hardness under trace-based, spectral, and operator metrics across broad approximation thresholds.
Extend trace-based identity hardness to circuits using only classical-reversible gates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical hardness proofs, including all non-trivial thresholds for specified trace-based cases, rather than empirical benchmarks or hardware evaluations.
watch_item: Worst-case PP-hardness does not rule out effective heuristics on practical circuits, and threshold coverage depends on the target set and metric.
paper_title: On the Hardness of Approximate Quantum Circuit Membership and Optimization
